title: Consolidate model loader format adapters and improve sharded checkpoint compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Over time we accumulated multiple ad-hoc adapters in the model loader to support different checkpoint formats (legacy .bin float32, bf16, multiple quantized variants, and per-shard manifests). These adapters have diverged: code duplication, inconsistent memory accounting, and subtle bugs around KV-cache initialization and tokenizer->vocab coupling. Goal: replace the ad-hoc adapters with a single, small compatibility layer and a strict loader pipeline that standardizes a canonical in-memory weight representation and a pluggable tokenizer interface. Expected outcomes: smaller code surface, reproducible load paths, 30-50% faster cold model load on common checkpoints, less OOM risk when loading multi-shard models, and easier path to supporting new quantized formats.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce weight-format adapter registry with well-documented interface
Canonical in-memory weight representation documented and used by runtime
Sharded checkpoint loader supports streaming per-shard deserialization and KV-cache warmup hooks
Tokenizer import decoupled from model config; support for external tokenizer override via loader API
Unit/integration tests covering legacy formats (.bin float32, bf16, int8-qs8) and a synthetic sharded checkpoint
Benchmark showing >=30% reduction in median cold load time for 7B and 13B models on dedicated infra
Rollout plan for canarying changes on dedicated pools and a rollback procedure
technical_notes: Work split: 1) design adapter registry and canonical weight layout (byte layout + shape metadata) 2) implement streaming shard reader that consumes manifests and exposes async chunk iterators 3) refactor tokenizer boot sequence so TokenizerLoader is injected and not side-effecting global state 4) add compatibility decoders for older checkpoint layouts and verify against our conversion scripts. Tradeoffs: a fully lazy weight mapping (mmap-like) would be ideal but is blocked by variance in quantized file formats; instead we implement chunked deserialization + eviction-friendly buffers. Memory accounting hooks added to runtime to avoid transient duplicates during conversion. Security: ensure loader does not execute untrusted code; sandbox manifest parsing and ban custom loader deserializers unless signed.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Design doc + API sketch in Confluence; prototype registry (ENG-9581-PROTOTYPE branch)
Week 2: Implement streaming shard reader and add synthetic sharded checkpoint tests
Week 3: Implement adapters for float32, bf16, and int8-qs8 and wire into runtime
Week 4: Perf tuning, add memory accounting, integration tests, and run benchmarks
Week 5: Internal code review, security review, and prepare canary rollout in dedicated pool
Week 6: Canary monitoring and bake, then gradual rollout to hosted and private targets
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: New loader could regress cold-start latency for some quantized formats. Mitigation: maintain old loader behind a feature flag and benchmark both on variety of hardware.
Risk: Tokenizer decoupling could break models that relied on implicit side effects. Mitigation: run compatibility suite against all prod models and provide fallback that logs a deprecation warning.
Risk: Sharded streaming increases I/O pressure. Mitigation: add per-host concurrency caps, prefetch heuristics, and in-memory LRU for recently accessed chunk buffers.

notes_for_release_notes: Consolidates multiple legacy model-loading code paths into a single, tested pipeline. Expected to reduce cold-start times for many models. Will be rolled out behind a feature flag and can be disabled if regressions are observed. Private deployment bundles may need a brief compatibility check for custom checkpoint layouts.
